content:
The shape that isn’t a Platonic solid is the **d10** – the **pentagonal trapezohedron**.

**Why?**  

The common “polyhedral dice” listed under the “common variations of dice shapes” are:

| Die (polyhedron) | Number of faces | Polyhedron type |
|------------------|----------------|-----------------|
| d4               | 4              | Tetrahedron (Platonic) |
| d6               | 6              | Cube (Platonic) |
| d8               | 8              | Octahedron (Platonic) |
| d10              | 10             | **Pentagonal trapezohedron** (Catalan solid) |
| d12              | 12             | Dodecahedron (Platonic) |
| d20              | 20             | Icosahedron (Platonic) |

The five Platonic solids are the tetrahedron, cube, octahedron, dodecahedron, and icosahedron. The **pentagonal trapezohedron** (used for the ten‑sided die) does not belong to this set; it is one of the Catalan solids, the dual of the pentagonal icositetrahedron. Therefore, among the shapes listed, the **d10** is the one that is **not a Platonic solid**.
